plan.title: bug(hooks): warn when a fail-closed hook registration travels without a hostable runtime

narratives.Description: Directive git-tracks the fail-closed Cursor hook registration while gitignoring the runtime it names. The registration travels via git; the implementation does not. Any clone, CI runner, or container without a global npm install fail-closes every mutation at exit 127 with no in-session recovery. This scope warns at the one moment a runtime is provably present, and documents the durable out-of-band recovery.
narratives.Overview:
## Bound remedy and what this scope covers

The #3785 bind comment `5455783077` carries the operator-ratified Stop 5 verified-claims table and a four-item bound remedy. Fail-open-on-absence was refuted 3/3 as unimplementable and as an escalation primitive; `failClosed: true` stays.

This scope delivers bound items **3** and **4**, plus the acceptance clause that locks fail-closed on. Bound items **1** and **2** are split out on cross-platform evidence gathered during this scope (see Out of scope).

## Item 4 -- warn when the registration travels without its runtime

The reachability condition for the lockout is: an agent-hook registration file is git-tracked while nothing in the tree lets a clone obtain the `deft-hook` runtime. The committed `package.json` pin on `@deftai/directive` (#2264) is the existing reconstitution anchor -- with it, a clone can install the runtime; without it, the registration names a command that no clone can host.

Deposit and update warn on that pairing. Cursor is named specifically because it is the only host deposited `failClosed: true`, so it is the only host where a missing runtime denies rather than fails open.

Warn-only, never fail-closed: refusing `deft update` on this condition would itself be a lockout.

## Item 3 -- document the out-of-band recovery

Recovery docs lead with `deft policy:disable-host-hooks --host cursor --confirm` (`plan.policy.hostHooks.cursor = false`). They state explicitly that hand-editing `failClosed: false` in the deposited `.cursor/hooks.json` works once and is silently reverted by the next `deft update`, which re-arms the lockout. Two critics found that upgrade trap independently in the reporter's own repository history.

Absent, crashed, and timed-out are recorded as one non-decision class: the hook exit contract already renders every verdict as exit 0 with a JSON body, so every non-zero exit is by construction a non-decision. That answers the question left open on #3736 at `5431700487` rather than re-deriving it.

## Legibility through the channel that provably travels

A no-Node host cannot run any Directive verb, so a documented CLI recovery is a note to a human outside the session. AGENTS.md is tracked and travels with the clone, so the locked-out session can still read it. A managed card names the exit-127 signature and the recovery, so the agent reports the exact remedy instead of guessing. Mirrored into `content/templates/agents-entry.md` per #1309.

## Out of scope -- split on portability evidence

Bound items 1 (hostable no-Node runtime) and 2 (wrapper that renders an explicit deny with a decision code) both require the deposited `command` string to name a repo-local runner. Measured during this scope:

- `cmd.exe` cannot execute a forward-slash relative path as the command token (`'.deft' is not recognized`); backslashes work but break POSIX `sh`.
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 has no `&&` / `||`, so a compound fallback command string is a parse error there.
- Cursor shell-evaluates the command through the host shell, which is PowerShell on Windows and `sh` on Linux, and third-party guidance states shebang scripts do not work on Windows.

A single tracked `hooks.json` therefore cannot name a repo-local runner portably. Delivering items 1 and 2 needs a per-platform command token, which is a deposit-architecture decision (per-machine untracked registration, or a PATH-installed shim), not a code change inside this scope. Shipping a POSIX-only registration would lock out Windows consumers -- the same failure class this issue reports.

## Acceptance

See clauses. Items 1 and 2 of the #3785 acceptance list stay open on the split issue; this scope does not claim them.

Refs #3785, #3736, #3732, #3742, #3156, #2752, #3100, #3801, #3571, #2264.
